newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE sees 19.2 MT Australia 97/98 wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE sees 19.2 MT Australia 97/98 wheat crop.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has boosted its official forecast of Australia's 1997/98 wheat crop to almost 19.2 million tonnes from the previous forecast of 17.82 million tonnes.
In its latest Australian Crop Report publication, ABARE said continued strong wheat prices were likely to result in the second largest wheat area planted in a decade.

The Australian wheat area was expected to be 11.1 million hectares for the 1997/98 (April-March) crop, down two percent from 1996/97 when Australia produced a record wheat crop of 23.586 million tonnes.
The 19.164 million tonne wheat crop forecast for 1997/98 was based on current planting intentions and assuming normal rainfall through to harvest, ABARE said.
ABARE's previous wheat forecast was issued in its March Australian Commodities bulletin.
The previous Crop Report, issued in February, forecast the 1997/98 wheat crop at 16.98 million tonnes.

ABARE said on Tuesday that with good rainfall received in May and low returns for feed barley, wheat plantings in the state of New South Wales (NSW) were expected to reach 3.4 million ha, the same area sown in 1996/97.

Western Australia (WA) had had an ideal start to the season but wheat plantings were expected to decrease as farmers planted crops likely to provide a higher return. The state's wheat area is forecast to fall by six percent to 4.1 million ha.
Queensland's wheat area is forecast to increase by 10 percent to 1.1 million ha, mainly from increased plantings in central parts of the state.
However, if dry conditions persisted in South Australia (SA) and Victoria, farmers might opt to plant more wheat and barley instead of higher returning crops, ABARE said.
ABARE forecasts that WA would emerge as Australia's biggest wheat-producing state in 1997/98, overtaking NSW.
WA is forecast to produce 6.64 million tonnes of wheat against 6.29 million tonnes in NSW. In 1996/97, NSW produced 8.62 million tonnes of wheat against 7.70 million tonnes in WA.
ABARE forecasts that Australian wheat exports would decline in 1997/98, to 14.50 million tonnes from 19.42 million tonnes the year before.
Stocks were predicted to decline to 326,000 tonnes from 656,000 tonnes.
